defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: expanduser(f"~/{name}") prepends ~/ to absolute NETRC path, file not found, returns None
Empty NETRC env var not treated as unset, prevents fallback to default netrc files
Tests only cover relative NETRC path; add absolute, empty, and non-existent cases
votes.evidence_quote: `os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}")` blindly prepends `~/` even when `name` is an absolute path. With `NETRC="/etc/custom_netrc"`, the formatted string becomes `"~//etc/custom_netrc"`, which expands to `/home/user//etc/custom_netrc` — a non-existent path, so the function silently returns `None` instead of reading the file the user specified.
votes.justification: The first finding names the expanduser call in get_netrc_auth and gives the same cause: an absolute NETRC path gets the ~/ prefix. It also gives the same result: the file is not found and None is returned.
